# bugs #4233: (unsigned char)(nh << 1) passed to a wider parameter arrives as 0x0100

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4233/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Decide between this patch and the ticket's patch, which also keeps casts that the compiler adds. Then apply and close.
- Patch: [bugs-4233.patch](../../patches/bugs-4233.patch), commit [`66b6358a5`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/66b6358a506a7c7f881b4f8ed1d6fa763666bbdd). Applies to r17192 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 the program in the ticket passes 0x0100 to `sink` for `(unsigned char)(nh << 1)`. The
value must be 0. For mcs51 the program was linked with a `sink` that stores its argument, and it
was run in ucsim. `sink` receives 0x0100 in the small model, in the small model with
`--stack-auto`, and in the medium model. It receives 0 in the large model, with and without
`--stack-auto`. With `static` in the declaration of `nh`, it receives 0 in the small model. For
z80 and stm8 the program was compiled and not run. Their assembly shifts 16 bits and sign-extends
the result to 64 bits. pic16, where the reporter found the problem, was not built.

More arguments were run for mcs51 in the small model. These arrive with a wrong value:

- `(typeof (nh))(nh << 1)` and `(unsigned char)(nh + nh)` arrive as 0x0100.
- `(signed char)(sh << 2)` arrives as 0x0100 when the `signed char` object `sh` is 0x40.
- `(unsigned char)~nv` arrives as 0xffffffffffffffff, and `(unsigned char)-nh` arrives as
  0xffffffffffffff80.
- `(unsigned char)(nh << 1)` arrives as 0x0100 when the parameter is `unsigned long` or
  `unsigned int`.
- `(unsigned char)(nh << 1) == 0` arrives as 0, and the correct value is 1.

These arrive with the correct value: `(volatile unsigned char)(nh << 1)`, the shift of a `volatile`
object, `(unsigned char)(nh * 2)`, `(unsigned char)(nh << 1) + 1ull`,
`(unsigned long long)(unsigned char)(nh << 1)`, and an `unsigned long long` object after the
assignment of `(unsigned char)(nh << 1)`.

## Cause

The cause is the one that the ticket describes. `processParms` in `src/SDCCast.c` calls
`decorateType` for the argument. For the operand of the cast, `decorateType` uses the result type
`char`, and `computeType` returns a copy of the type of `nh` as the type of the shift.
`compareTypeExact` finds this type equal to the type of the cast, and `decorateType` returns the
shift node without the `CAST` node.

The argument then has the type `unsigned char` and needs a conversion to the type of the
parameter. `processParms` copies the argument with `copyAst`, makes the copy the operand of an
implicit `CAST` node, and calls `decorateType` for that node. `copyAst` does not copy the
`decorated` flag. `decorateType` therefore computes the type of the shift again, with the result
type of the parameter, and the shift becomes an `int` operation.

`compareTypeExact` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` also compares the `static` flag, the storage class, and the
qualifiers of the two types. The copy that `computeType` returns has the `static` flag and the
storage class of `nh`, and `allocGlobal` sets the storage class of `nh` to `xdata` in the large
model. In these cases, and for the `volatile` cast, `compareTypeExact` finds a difference and the
`CAST` node stays.

## Fix

With the patch, `decorateType` removes explicit casts between equal types only where the operand
is a symbol or a literal (`IS_AST_VALUE`). The type of symbols and literals does not depend on the
result type. Explicit casts of operations stay in the tree as `CAST` nodes. `geniCodeCast` returns
its operand for casts between equal types, so these nodes do not generate code.

## Decision

The patch in the ticket removes the cast only where its operand is a value node. This patch has
that condition and one more: casts that the compiler added (`implicitCast`) are removed as in
trunk. The code that adds such a cast adds it again whenever a copy of the tree is decorated, so
the conversion is kept. The patch in the ticket was not applied or tested here.

The patch does not change the code size of the other regression tests for the six mcs51 variants,
stm8, and ucz80.

One cost was read from the code and not measured. `isShiftRightLitVal_BitAndLitVal` looks for the
shift directly below the `&`. Where a `CAST` node stays between a right shift and `& 1`, the
function does not match, and the bit is not extracted with the `GETABIT` operation. Where the
operand of the shift is `static`, the cast stays without the patch as well.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4233.c` has 13 assertions on objects that are not `static`. Without
the rest of the patch, all 13 fail on r17192 for mcs51-small and mcs51-small-stack-auto, and all
pass for mcs51-large. On r17176 all 13 also failed for mcs51-medium, stm8, and ucz80, and all
passed for mcs51-huge and mcs51-large-stack-auto. With the patch the test passes for the host, the
six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80.

With the patch on r17176, the program of the ticket passes 0 to `sink` in ucsim for mcs51 in the
small model. pic16 was not built.

## Related

The cast removal in `decorateType` is also the cause of bugs #3674 and #3172. The fork has a patch
for them in `processParms`, and the two patches do not conflict. With this patch applied and the
change in `processParms` reverted, the tests `bug-3674` and `bug-3172` pass on four mcs51 variants.

`char *p = (char *)(buf + 1);` at file scope is rejected as not constant for mcs51 in the large
model, stm8, and z80. The patch does not cause it, and it was not examined.
